scenes.caption: Photo 1889
scenes.text: Many slaves were shipped through Goree to the Dutch colony of Curaçao in the 1660s and 70s.

scenes.caption: Photo 1889
scenes.text: After the French invasion in 1677, during the Franco-Dutch War, the island remained chiefly French until 1960.

scenes.caption: Photo 1900
scenes.text: After the decline of the slave trade from Senegal in the 1770s and 1780s, the town became an important port for the shipment of peanuts, peanut oil, gum arabic, ivory, and other products of the "legitimate" trade.

scenes.caption: Photo 1905
scenes.text: In February 1794 during the French Revolution, France abolished slavery, and the slave trade from Senegal was said to have stopped.

scenes.caption: Photo 1910
scenes.text: In the 18th and 19th century, Gorée was home to a Franco-African Creole, or Métis, community of merchants with links to similar communities in Saint-Louis and the Gambia, and across the Atlantic to France's colonies in the…

scenes.caption: Photo 1839
scenes.text: Civic franchise for the citizens of Gorée was institutionalized in 1872, when it became a French commune with an elected mayor and a municipal council.

scenes.caption: Photo 1889
scenes.text: Blaise Diagne, the first African deputy elected to the French National Assembly (served 1914 to 1934), was born on Gorée.

scenes.caption: Photo 1889
scenes.text: The Dakar-Gorée Swim was launched in 1985 as a homage to the victims of slavery who displayed resilience by attempting to swim towards freedom.

scenes.caption: Photo 1900
scenes.text: The current mayor of Gorée is Augustin Senghor, elected in 2002.

scenes.title: The place
scenes.text: An island off Dakar, a trading post fought over by the Portuguese, Dutch, British and French, and a place of memory of the Atlantic slave trade. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1978.
